node.title: Replace roster damage heuristic with construction maxima
acceptance: First characterize a unit with armor damage but no destroyed component/location at the real roster-card boundary.
Resolve matching construction maxima through the established canonical/custom source authority; missing maxima remain explicitly unavailable without stock substitution or fabricated percentages.
Calculate the displayed damage from current armor/structure against matching maxima; preserve readiness as a separate projection and prove reactive updates.
Admit exact bounded files and regression before implementation; independent review, focused/static/build/browser gates, incremental PR, guarded merge, exact-main verification and owned cleanup.

currentHeuristic.function: computeDamageBarData, lines 116-136 (called by useDamageBarData, lines 151-179, called by RosterUnitCard, line 196)
currentHeuristic.arithmetic: totalDamage = destroyedCount * 2 + destroyedLocationCount * 4 (line 126), where destroyedCount = combatState.destroyedComponents.length (line 121) and destroyedLocationCount = combatState.destroyedLocations.length (line 122). Displayed bar width = `Math.min(100, damageBar.totalDamage * 5)%` (line 230).
currentHeuristic.inputsRead: Only IUnitCombatState.destroyedComponents.length and IUnitCombatState.destroyedLocations.length. Never reads currentArmorPerLocation or currentStructurePerLocation values, and never reads any construction-maxima reference (no IUnitMaxState companion is consulted anywhere in this file today).
currentHeuristic.displayGate: The entire damage-bar block (lines 223-235) is gated on `damageBar.totalDamage > 0`. Because totalDamage is derived only from destroyed-item counts, a unit with real armor/structure point loss but zero destroyed components/locations yields totalDamage=0, so the whole block is omitted from the DOM — the card renders visually identical to a fully healthy unit.
currentHeuristic.explicitCodeComment: RosterStateCards.tsx:92-99 (IDamageBarData.totalDamage doc): 'Crude total-damage proxy used by the legacy display-bar width calculation. Without an `IUnitMaxState` companion we approximate "how damaged" with destroyed component + location counts. Repair tickets diff against the max-state for accurate values; this is a display heuristic only.'
currentHeuristic.corroboratingSourceOfTruth: openspec/specs/campaign-unit-combat-state/spec.md line 244 (Migration status item 3, marked 'Not closed'): '`RosterStateCards.tsx` selects canonical `IUnitCombatState` from `campaign.unitCombatStates[unitId]`, but `computeDamageBarData` still uses the destroyed-component/location heuristic (`destroyedCount * 2 + destroyedLocationCount * 4`) because the card has no `IUnitMaxState` companion. ... This remaining heuristic is `R9.roster-damage` after `R2.camp-7`.'
currentHeuristic.sameRootCauseElsewhere_notInScope: The identical root cause (readiness/damage can't be told apart from armor numbers without a max-state companion) was independently hit and hand-patched for the READINESS badge (a different, out-of-scope code path) in src/stores/campaign/campaignRosterStore.helpers.ts, function `deriveReadinessFromCarryForward` (lines 152-198): comment at lines 140-144 states 'the helper can't see armor deltas without a max-state companion, so this bridges that gap' — it bumps a computed 'Ready' to 'Damaged' when a battle's raw armor/structure damage totals are nonzero. This bridge is NOT applied to the live roster-card selector's own totalDamage computation (RosterStateCards.tsx has no equivalent), and it is NOT in this node's ownershipPaths — cited only as independent proof the exact same defect class has already surfaced once before in this codebase.

maximaSource.typeAlreadyExists: IUnitMaxState (src/types/campaign/UnitCombatState.ts:109-118): `maxArmorPerLocation`, `maxStructurePerLocation`, `maxAmmoPerBin`, all `Readonly<Record<string, number>>`. Doc comment (lines 101-108) states it is 'the "full health" reference state for a unit, used by the repair queue builder to diff against current `IUnitCombatState`' and 'Source of truth: the unit's construction state at deploy time.'
maximaSource.alreadyWiredIntoCampaign: `ICampaign.unitMaxStates?: Readonly<Record<string, IUnitMaxState>>` (src/types/campaign/Campaign.ts:162) is already optional on the campaign shape, already round-trips through persistence (src/lib/campaign/persistence/serializeCampaign.ts:166,236; src/stores/campaign/useCampaignStore.persistence.ts:127,288,381; src/types/campaign/SerializedCampaign.ts:194), and is already read (never written) by src/lib/campaign/repair/repairQueueBuilder.ts:140-195, src/lib/campaign/processors/repairQueueBuilderProcessor.ts:97, src/lib/campaign/processors/repairProgressProcessor.ts:100/149/201/226, and src/lib/campaign/fastForward/invariants/maintenance.ts:81-90. No schema or type change is needed to add a reader in RosterStateCards.tsx.
maximaSource.criticalGap_neverPopulatedInProduction: grep across src/ (excluding __tests__) for every reference to `unitMaxStates` and to the only production constructor of combat state, `createInitialCombatState` (UnitCombatState.ts:79-96, called only from src/lib/campaign/processors/postBattleProcessor.helpers.ts:184), found ZERO production call sites that ever WRITE `campaign.unitMaxStates[unitId]`. Every non-test reference is either the type declaration, a pass-through in serialize/deserialize, or a read with its own 'absent → skip' branch (e.g. repairQueueBuilder.ts:158-160's 'Absent max-state entry' scenario, or maintenance.ts:81 'A unit with no `unitMaxStates` entry is skipped'). In today's production code, `campaign.unitMaxStates` is always undefined/empty for every real roster unit — the repair-ticket diff and maintenance-cap consumers of this field are exercising their own no-op/skip branches against live data, not the diff branch.
maximaSource.establishedCanonicalCustomAuthority_asyn: The actual construction-maxima VALUES are resolved elsewhere, but only on the async combat-LAUNCH path, never at roster-card render time: `adaptUnitFromData` (src/engine/adapters/CompendiumAdapter.ts:84-104) derives per-location max armor via `extractArmor(unitData.armor.allocation)` (line 97-98) and max structure via `getStructureForTonnage(tonnage)` (line 103). The dispatcher `adaptUnit` (CompendiumAdapter.ts:167-190) routes `custom-*` refs through a `CustomUnitDefinitionReader` (browser default `customUnitApiService.getById`, CompendiumAdapter.ts:190-192; server-side `readServerCustomCombatDefinition`, src/services/units/serverCustomCombatDefinition.ts:22-42, backed by the SQLite `UnitRepository`) and canonical refs through `getCanonicalUnitService().getById` (src/services/units/CanonicalUnitService.ts:215, itself an async `fetch()`-backed lookup, CanonicalUnitService.ts:157-166). Both paths throw or return null on a missing/invalid definition rather than substituting a stock unit (CompendiumAdapter.ts:170-176; EncounterService.ts comment at line 419+ 'custom units never [skip] — missing or invalid construction fails the launch'). This whole resolution chain runs only from `deriveCombatSeededGameUnits` (src/engine/combatSeedDerivation.ts:48-72), called from `EncounterService.launchEncounter` — i.e. at combat launch, not at roster display or roster-add time.
maximaSource.missingDesignPrecedentElsewhereInRosterD: src/lib/campaign/bays/resolveMechBayUnit.ts, `resolveMechBayLoadout` (lines 44-49): when a roster unit's `unitSource` is 'custom' and its saved design id is not found in the caller-supplied `savedDesigns` map, the resolver adds the unit to `unresolvedUnitIds` and falls back only to a previously-cached scalar (tonnage) — it does not fabricate a value or silently substitute canonical data. This is the exact 'missing maxima remain explicitly unavailable' shape the roadmap acceptance line 2 asks for, already established as a convention in a sibling roster file (not in this node's ownershipPaths, cited as the pattern to mirror).
maximaSource.resolutionForThisBoundedSlice: Given (a) the type and the ICampaign field already exist with zero schema changes needed, and (b) no production writer for `unitMaxStates` exists and building one is out of this node's 3-file ownershipPaths / 5-file cap (it would touch the roster-add flow and/or combat-launch wiring across several additional files, which is exactly the 'persistence/authority redesign' the decomposition note rules out), the bounded fix in this slice can only be a READER change: compute the damage percentage from `campaign.unitCombatStates[unitId]` against `campaign.unitMaxStates?.[unitId]` when present, and render an explicit 'unavailable' state when absent (mirroring resolveMechBayLoadout's unresolved-fallback shape and repairQueueBuilder.ts's per-location 'absent → skip' loop, CompendiumAdapter- and repairQueueBuilder-style, lines 150-153: `current = state.currentArmorPerLocation[location] ?? maxArmor`). This is an honest, non-fabricating fix that removes the wrong 0%-looks-healthy heuristic. It does NOT, by itself, make the card show a real percentage for any unit in production today, because nothing populates `unitMaxStates` yet — see dependencyNote and openQuestions below; this is flagged for the parent rather than silently assumed.

failingCase.reproduction: Given `combatState = { currentArmorPerLocation: { CT: 5, LT: 8 }, currentStructurePerLocation: {}, destroyedComponents: [], destroyedLocations: [], combatReady: true, ... }` (e.g. CT armor reduced from a true max of 30 to 5, LT from 20 to 8, with no critical/component destruction), `computeDamageBarData` (RosterStateCards.tsx:116-136) returns `{ totalDamage: 0, hasDestroyedComponents: false, destroyedCount: 0, destroyedNames: [] }`. The gate at line 223 (`damageBar.totalDamage > 0`) is false, so the entire damage-bar block is omitted — the card is visually indistinguishable from a unit at full armor/structure.

readiness.separateProjectionConfirmed: `getReadinessStyles` (RosterStateCards.tsx:36-50) and the 'Needs Repair' block (lines 248-268) both key exclusively off `unit.readiness`, a field on `IRosterUnitProjection` (src/types/campaign/RosterUnitProjection.ts:112) computed by `deriveRosterReadiness` (RosterUnitProjection.ts:142-158) and, at roster-add/carry-forward time, by the store-side bridge `deriveReadinessFromCarryForward` (src/stores/campaign/campaignRosterStore.helpers.ts:152-198, sole production caller confirmed by grep). Neither function is in this node's ownershipPaths, and the damage-bar fix touches a structurally separate function/hook (`computeDamageBarData`/`useDamageBarData`) with no shared state — confirmed by reading the full 398-line component file: `unit.readiness` and `damageBar` are two independent props/hooks consumed by `RosterUnitCard` with no data dependency between them.
readiness.reactivityMechanism: `useDamageBarData` (RosterStateCards.tsx:151-179) already subscribes to the live campaign store via `useStore(storeApi, selector)` with a hand-rolled shallow-equality memo (lines 163-171) so the card only re-renders when the four selected fields actually change. The bounded fix extends the SAME selector to also read `state.campaign?.unitMaxStates?.[unitId]` inside the existing subscription — no new store, no new subscription, no new re-render source. Reactivity is proven by test 2 above (mutate the mock store via `act(() => store.setState(...))`, assert the rendered value changes) rather than by inspection alone.

boundedFiles.purpose: Replace `computeDamageBarData`'s destroyed-count arithmetic with a real percentage computed from `IUnitCombatState.currentArmorPerLocation`/`currentStructurePerLocation` against `IUnitMaxState.maxArmorPerLocation`/`maxStructurePerLocation` when present (per-location diff loop mirroring repairQueueBuilder.ts:150-153's `current ?? max` pattern, summed across locations named in the max-state — locations absent from the max-state are skipped, matching the existing 'Absent max-state entry' convention). Add an explicit 'unavailable' branch when no max-state entry exists for the unit. Extend `useDamageBarData`'s selector (lines 159-174) to also read `state.campaign?.unitMaxStates?.[unitId]`. Do not touch `getReadinessStyles`, `getPilotStatusStyles`, or `RosterPilotCard`.

nonClaims: Does NOT add a production population pipeline for `campaign.unitMaxStates` — confirmed no such writer exists today (see maximaSource.criticalGap_neverPopulatedInProduction). Building one would touch the roster-add flow and/or combat-launch wiring across additional files beyond this node's 3-file ownershipPaths and is exactly the 'persistence/authority redesign' the decomposition note excludes. Until a companion population task lands, the fixed card will show the new explicit 'maxima unavailable' state for real production units rather than a real percentage — an honest regression-free improvement over today's silently-wrong-or-hidden heuristic, not a full visual fix.

Does NOT change `unit.readiness`, `deriveRosterReadiness`, or `deriveReadinessFromCarryForward` — readiness stays exactly as computed today, including its own pre-existing, separately-owned heuristic gap (readiness also can't distinguish 'damaged by armor loss alone' from 'ready' without a max-state companion, per RosterUnitProjection.ts:130-135's own comment) which this node does not touch or claim to fix.

Does NOT substitute a stock/canonical unit's maxima for a missing custom design, and does NOT fabricate a percentage when maxima are unknown — the absent-maxima branch renders an explicit unavailable affordance, mirroring resolveMechBayLoadout's unresolved-fallback pattern.
Does NOT touch `RosterPilotCard`, pilot wounds/recovery display, or any other card in this file beyond the unit damage bar.
Does NOT weaken or extend the existing `IUnitMaxState`/`ICampaign.unitMaxStates` schema — both already exist with the exact fields needed; only a new reader is added.
Does NOT claim the underlying data-population gap is this node's to close — flagged explicitly to the parent as an open dependency (see openQuestions).
